# Changelog

## v2.10.0

- ADD Firewall Manager 0.5.0 zavádí první explicitní mutační workflow UFW. Lokální `firewall.json` se kompiluje do vlastněných OpenVPN BAN/izolačních, Hard Source Allow a nového Standard Firewall bloku; běžná INPUT/OUTPUT/FORWARD pravidla podporují allow/drop/reject, protokol, src/dst CIDR, zdrojové/cílové porty a interface.
- SAFE Apply je pouze ruční z menu. Kandidát zachovává všechny nespravované řádky, před zápisem se semanticky kontroluje a generated akce procházejí `iptables-restore --test` / `ip6tables-restore --test`. Po atomickém zápisu proběhne `ufw --dry-run reload|enable` ještě před živou změnou.
- SAFE Před reload/enable se vytvoří úplná lokální záloha dotčených UFW souborů a aktivuje se nezávislý transient systemd rollback timer. Pokud správce po živé změně nepotvrdí funkční spojení, Apply se odmítne, proces selže nebo se spojení přeruší, původní soubory a původní active/inactive stav se obnoví.
- ADD Neaktivní UFW nabízí pouze chráněnou akci Aktivovat + Apply; aktivní UFW nabízí samostatný guarded Apply a explicitně potvrzované Disable. `NO_CHANGE` na aktivním firewallu neprovádí zápis ani reload.
- ADD IPv4 je spravováno v `before.rules`; pokud existuje `before6.rules`, family-neutral/IPv6 standardní pravidla se kompilují také do IPv6. Explicitní IPv6 pravidlo bez dostupného `before6.rules` failuje před změnou systému.
- SAFE Hub provider a hodinový Hub sync zůstávají striktně read-only vůči UFW; žádný automatický Apply není v 2.10.0 povolen. Fyzický enable/apply/rollback/disable test je určen pro testovací VM před jakýmkoli produkčním takeoverem.

replacements.old:
### Firewall Manager (UFW) — desired-state editor, UFW runtime still read-only

- Versioned local `/etc/jb_sys_apps/firewall.json` supports standard INPUT/FORWARD/OUTPUT rules, source/destination IP/CIDR, TCP/UDP source and destination ports, and interfaces.
- VPN BAN management is server-scoped: select an OpenVPN server, then manage only that server's BAN rules and expiry.
- Wizards reuse JBLibs `select/get_input/printBlock/confirm`, redraw accepted values as input progresses, and discover live host interfaces.
- Read-only inspection supports multiple managed OpenVPN blocks plus the Hard Source Allow block and deterministic dry-run comparison.
- Hub schema 008 synchronizes host-local VPN servers and rules only; central/group/all scope remains outside the host collector.
- This release does not enable UFW, reload it, or apply firewall changes; activation/rollback remains separate future work.
replacements.new:
### Firewall Manager (UFW) — desired-state editor + guarded manual Apply

- Versioned local `/etc/jb_sys_apps/firewall.json` supports standard INPUT/FORWARD/OUTPUT rules, source/destination IP/CIDR, TCP/UDP source and destination ports, and interfaces.
- VPN BAN management is server-scoped: select an OpenVPN server, then manage only that server's BAN rules and expiry.
- Preview and Apply use the same pure compiler. SysApps owns only marked OpenVPN, Hard Source Allow and Standard Firewall blocks while preserving all unrelated `before.rules` / `before6.rules` content.
- Manual Apply creates a backup, pre-arms an independent systemd rollback, validates generated actions and UFW dry-run, performs atomic file replacement, then reloads or guarded-enables UFW.
- The administrator must acknowledge that the management connection survived the live change; missing/rejected acknowledgement or any failure restores the previous files and previous active/inactive state automatically.
- Active `NO_CHANGE` performs no write/reload; Disable is a separate confirmed operation.
- Hub schema 008 synchronizes host-local VPN servers/rules, but Hub/hourly synchronization never auto-applies UFW in this release.

Config v2 owns a `vpn_servers` catalog with stable `server_id` plus rules that may reference it through `vpn_server_id`. replacements.old:
- UFW runtime remains **read-only**: `policy.py` is pure, `hub_provider.py` calls only UFW status/version, comparison only reads `before.rules`. No UFW reload, no write to `/etc/ufw`, no remote Apply.
- Pure `reconcile.py` only classifies plan against verified prior `applied_hash`; never mutates prior state or advances `last_applied_at`. Missing prior hash needs review; unexpected drift blocks automatic Apply. This release has NO persistent state and NO UFW Apply.
- Future Apply belongs to a separate guarded and tested implementation.
  It must stage+validate candidate config, arm automatic rollback before
  applying, verify new remote access and rollback on missing acknowledgement.
replacements.new:
- `policy.py` and `compiler.py` remain pure. `hub_provider.py` calls only UFW status/version and MUST remain read-only. All filesystem/service mutation is isolated in `apply.py`; no Hub collector, hourly sync or remote policy callback may import/call the mutator.
- Manual Apply must preserve unrelated UFW lines, stage/validate deterministic candidates, back up every touched file, arm an independent time-limited rollback before live activation, run UFW dry-run validation, apply atomically, require live management acknowledgement and verify candidate hashes before committing local apply state.
- An active `NO_CHANGE` is zero-write/zero-reload. A failed/rejected/unacknowledged Apply restores both touched files and the previous UFW active/inactive state. Do not weaken this for convenience.
- Automatic Hub/hourly Apply remains forbidden in 0.5.0. `reconcile.py` stays a decision-only layer until a separately reviewed opt-in unattended contract is implemented.

replacements.old: - Preserve deployed legacy BOF/EOF ownership and order. Multiple uniquely identified OpenVPN BAN/forward-isolation blocks are allowed and all must precede the single ZLKL Hard Source Allow block. Duplicate OpenVPN marker identities, duplicate Hard Source blocks, nested/unmatched markers or reversed ordering MUST fail closed. A VPN preview must use that server's configured interface, not silently fall back to `tun+`.
replacements.new: - Preserve deployed legacy BOF/EOF ownership and order. Multiple uniquely identified OpenVPN BAN/forward-isolation blocks are allowed and all must precede the single ZLKL Hard Source Allow block; the SysApps Standard Firewall block follows it. Duplicate identities/blocks, nested/unmatched markers or reversed ordering MUST fail closed. A VPN preview/apply must use that server's configured interface, not silently fall back to `tun+`.
